title: On Fighting the fire for two nights
subtitle: 战争和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：fight　|　正文 356 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fight 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 the fisherman ① fought the fire for two nights without a word of thanks, and every boatman in the harbour said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three seasons on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the fisherman ② fights the fire for two nights at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ fight the fire for two nights at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ fought the fire for two nights before — a line in the logbook for July 1944 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Fighting the fire for two nights without a word of thanks, the fisherman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the net at the far pier, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ fight for the bridge all through April at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Fight for the bridge all through April at once and never mention it again.

By 1957 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the logbook, and a new boatman from the next harbour ⑧ fights for the bridge all through April without a word of thanks every season without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the pier, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ fought the fire for two nights again when nobody else would.

⑩ To fight the fire for two nights, my mother said in 1962, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the harbour remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the harbour forgets, somebody fights the fire for two nights at once again and somebody must fight the fire for two nights without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 搏斗（一般过去式 fought the fire for two nights：1950 年渔人头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 搏斗（一般现在 fights the fire for two nights：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 搏斗（不定式 to fight the fire for two nights：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 搏斗（过去完成时 had fought the fire for two nights：1944 年七月的航海日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 搏斗（动名词 fighting the fire for two nights 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 作战（fight for the bridge all through April：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去作战整个四月为那座桥而战）
G. v. 作战（fight for the bridge all through April：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 搏斗（后段两处：新来的船工照例 fights for the bridge all through April，而母亲又一次 fought the fire for two nights）

fight 意为“搏斗”，自那以后渔人二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 fights。
fight 意为“搏斗”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯搏斗与那场火搏了两个晚上”，此处为不定式 to fight the fire for two nights。
fight 意为“搏斗”，航海日志里 七月 那行字说明早在 1957 年之前就有人搏斗过，故用过去完成时 had fought。
fight 意为“搏斗”，渔人说“搏斗与那场火搏了两个晚上这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 fighting the fire for two nights 作主语。
fight 意为“作战”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去作战整个四月为那座桥而战”，should ever 之后用原形 fight for the bridge all through April。
fight 意为“作战”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻作战整个四月为那座桥而战（fight for the bridge all through April at once），以后再也不要提起。
fight 意为“搏斗”，新来的船工每个汛期都照例作战整个四月为那座桥而战，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 fights。
fight 意为“搏斗”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢搏斗与那场火搏了两个晚上，用一般过去式 fought 叙述。
fight 意为“搏斗”，结尾那句是母亲 1962 年的话：要搏斗与那场火搏了两个晚上，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和渔港记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 fight 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1950 the fisherman fought the fire for two nights without a word of thanks, and nobody in the harbour forgot it.
Even now the fisherman fights the fire for two nights at once whenever the harbour asks.
Fighting the fire for two nights without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever fight for the bridge all through April at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new boatman from the next harbour fights for the bridge all through April without a word of thanks every season, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother fought the fire for two nights again, and the harbour remembered that half.
